actions.action: Push a chopstick to the bottom of the soil or lift the pot to check whether it is dry
If the soil is dry deeper down, water thoroughly
Slide the cactus out of its pot and inspect the roots
Cut off any rotten roots with clean scissors
Repot the cactus into a smaller draining pot with a half cactus soil, half bark or perlite mix
After about a week, water only when the top half of the soil is dry
Take 2–3 segment cuttings, let them dry a day, then plant them in barely damp gritty mix
Move both plants off the cold glass to a bright spot at 15–20 °C, away from radiators
Check that the oxalis rhizomes are firm
Cut all oxalis foliage off and keep its soil nearly dry for 2–4 weeks
Resume light watering of the oxalis when new shoots appear

reason: The answer blames root rot and lists underwatering only as an alternative, burying the watering fix behind a check while its main advice (repot, withhold water for a week, keep the oxalis nearly dry) would leave already-thirsty plants drier.
